setup.angle_policy: Alpha in the primary report is wing-root angle. Use alpha_body=alpha_wing-incidence in the body frame; use alpha_wing directly in the wing frame.

primary_normalization.method: Wind-axis strip forces. Partial strips crossing2|y|/b=0.1 use their exposed span fraction; mesh sensitivity is required.

limitations: Prescribed rigid geometry; structural deflection and free-flight trim are not solved.
Steady accelerating-frame and instantaneous apparent-mass loads; unsteady circulation lag is not solved.
CDi and span efficiency use the frozen straight Trefftz wake; total CD and load balance use near-field forces, including CDi_near.

protocol: Three meshes25/50/100, wing angles4.7/8.8/12.9, primary Mach0.19 and archive mixed PG.
For each condition compare unchanged iw0 and explicit iw4 geometry in wing-fixed and body-fixed frames.
The body-fixed condition angle is alpha_w-4deg. No source properties are fitted.
Original pilot states may be reused only with matching modules, source, condition and immutable cache hashes.
This supplements the known swept-force mesh limitation; it does not claim mesh convergence.
limitations: These are explicit rigid reconstructions, not recovered original iw=4 ASW files.
The supplied iw=0 geometry, normal chord, section properties, shared physical beam index and joint station/offset are retained. Their primary-experiment discrepancies remain.
The primary root-leading-edge pivot is prescribed at x36.76in,z3.18in; it is not selected to improve agreement.
A global4deg wing rotation requires a different local normal-section twist on the swept beam; simply adding4deg to its section twist is not equivalent.
Rotating the body oppositely with the wing fixed gives an equivalent reference frame. Numerical force and local-load covariance still require actual solver checks.
Source Figure17.csv is inferred to trace primary Figure15; its three eta=.15 points include lower-surface interpolation, and three tip endpoints are drawn-curve values.
